# VelociBar

> VelociBar is a macOS menu bar app for scheduled internet connection tests, local history, and CSV export. Its guides explain speed tests, responsiveness, and how to document recurring connection problems.

## Product facts

- Requires macOS 26 or later. See the [App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/velocibar/id6756196355) for current availability and pricing.
- Scheduled tests run every 15, 30, or 60 minutes while the app is running and the Mac is awake. They are periodic samples, not uninterrupted monitoring.
- Automatic tests alternate Apple's networkQuality engine and a CDN download engine. Manual tests use the CDN engine.
- Tests generate internet traffic and can consume significant data or affect other network activity. They are active measurements, not passive observation.
- Results are stored locally and can be exported. Local history does not mean the test itself stays offline: it contacts external test servers.
- The current CSV fields are timestamp, source, is_error, download_mbps, latency_ms, duration_s, bytes_downloaded, and responsiveness_rpm. Older app versions may contain fewer fields.
- Compare results within the same engine. Apple latency_ms is derived from RPM; CDN latency_ms records initial HTTP response time. The engines use different responsiveness methods. Zero RPM can mean unmeasured; error records should be separated from successful tests.
- A history can show recurring slowdowns. It cannot alone prove deliberate ISP throttling, locate a bottleneck, establish a contract violation, or guarantee compensation.
- Speedtest and Fast.com remain useful for spot checks and include latency measurements. Some Speedtest clients also offer history and sharing. VelociBar adds integrated scheduling and local CSV export on a Mac.

## Blog guides

- [Internet lento por la noche](https://velocibar.app/blog/internet-lento-por-la-noche.html): causas de la congestión en hora pico y cómo comprobarla con una semana de pruebas programadas · [English](https://velocibar.app/en/blog/internet-slow-at-night.html)
- [Qué es el bufferbloat](https://velocibar.app/blog/que-es-bufferbloat.html): por qué las videollamadas se cortan con buena velocidad, cómo medir la responsividad (RPM) y cómo reducirla · [English](https://velocibar.app/en/blog/what-is-bufferbloat.html)
- [Documentar internet lento para tu ISP](https://velocibar.app/blog/reclamar-isp-internet-lento.html): pruebas comparables por cable, historial CSV y una solicitud clara a soporte, con los límites de lo que un historial demuestra · [English](https://velocibar.app/en/blog/prove-isp-throttling.html)
- [Test de velocidad en Mac](https://velocibar.app/blog/test-velocidad-mac.html): tres métodos, incluida la herramienta networkQuality de Apple en la Terminal y cómo leer su salida · [English](https://velocibar.app/en/blog/speed-test-mac.html)
- [Videollamadas que se cortan con un test de velocidad bueno](https://velocibar.app/blog/videollamadas-se-cortan-test-velocidad-bien.html): por qué importa la latencia bajo carga (responsividad, RPM) y no los Mbps, con cuatro ejecuciones reales de networkQuality en un Mac, cómo revisarlo en cinco minutos y qué lo soluciona · [English](https://velocibar.app/en/blog/video-calls-lag-speed-test-fine.html)
- [Speedtest vs Fast.com vs VelociBar](https://velocibar.app/blog/speedtest-vs-fastcom-vs-monitoreo-continuo.html): qué mide cada uno, cuándo usarlos y qué preguntas solo responde un historial · [English](https://velocibar.app/en/blog/speedtest-vs-fastcom-vs-continuous-monitoring.html)

Each article links to its Markdown equivalent, its translation, and its supporting sources.
